paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, and comparing the performance of six different model configurations. The horizontal axis represents nine language families, ordered as IE-Indic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "effect", displays values ranging from 0 to 30 on a linear scale with tick labels at intervals of 5. Six distinct bar groups represent the following model configurations: mBERT-L2 (light green), XLM-L2 (light blue), mBERT-R2 (red), XLM-R2 (teal), mBERT-B2 (dark green), and XLM-B2 (purple). Each bar includes an associated error bar indicating standard deviation. For example, in the IE-Indic language family, the mBERT-L2 configuration displays a bar with an approximate value of 3, while XLM-B2 reaches approximately 25. In the Uralic family, all model configurations are near zero effect.  The bars are sorted alphabetically by language family, and no visual emphasis is applied to any bars beyond the differentiating colors and error bars.
